newsitem.title: UK: most popular UK band since the Beatles?.
newsitem.headline: most popular UK band since the Beatles?.

text.p: British rock superstars Oasis, reported to have split up during a tour of the United States on Thursday, have been hyped as Britain's most popular band since the Beatles although they have only released two albums.
The driving force behind the Manchester quintet were the perpetually squabbling Gallagher brothers -- lead singer Liam and his older brother Noel, the songwriter and lead guitarist.
They swore, sneered, played tunes reminiscent of The Beatles and boasted they were the biggest thing since Jesus.

"We have sold more records than the Beatles, we've played bigger gigs than The Beatles and we're bigger than The Beatles," Noel crowed in a recent interview. "We are the biggest band in Britain of all time."
In Britain, Oasis trumped the Beatles in terms of a single audience by drawing a quarter of a million fans at an outdoor concert at Knebworth north of London in August.

The band sold around 15 million albums worldwide, generating around $250 million. Their second album, (What's the Story) Morning Glory, a polished selection of 12 neo-Beatles songs, sold three million copies in Britain alone.
(According to the Guinness Book of Records, The Beatles' world sales to date are estimated at more than one billion discs and tapes).

But success brought the inevitable pressures of modern fame. The Beatles would have been all too familiar with the obsessive interest the brothers generated, including infatuated fans camping outside their homes.
"You want to try to be me and Liam for an afternoon," Noel was recently quoted as saying. "You'd slit your throat."
It was 23-year-old Liam who showed signs of cracking up under the stress of the band's phenomenal success and the continuing rows with Noel, 29.
Just minutes before Oasis were due to record a secret acoustic concert in London last month for music channel MTV, Liam announced he would not perform because of a sore throat.

Three days later, he stormed out of Heathrow airport just before the band was due to fly to the United States for the 17-date make-or-break tour. He had decided that finding a new home with 28-year-old fiancee Patsy Kensit was more important.

"I'm f***ing fed up with not having a home, my throat hurts, my head hurts and I don't want to tour any more," he told reporters in typically forthright manner, in between sticking two fingers up at cameramen.
But he was soon back at Heathrow on his way to the United States for the ill-fated tour, designed to whip up the same kind of mania as they had done in Britain.
The U.S. tour has drawn far from rave reviews. At an MTV awards evening in New York, Liam spat and threw beer at the audience.
The brothers' goal had been to play New York's Shea stadium where The Beatles played their biggest American concert in August 1965 in front of an audience of 55,000.

The band first used the name Oasis in August 1991 and began their push for stardom when Noel joined the following year. Their first album, Definitely Maybe, was released in August 1994. What's the Story (Morning Glory)? followed last October.
